source.title: Temporal Dependencies in In-Context Learning: The Role of Induction Heads
source.authors: Anooshka Bajaj; Deven Mahesh Mistry; Sahaj Singh Maini; Y. Aggarwal; Billy Dickson; Zoran Tiganj

page_placements.theme: Retrieval heads in long-context retrieval, many-shot ICL and grounded generation

record.tranche_reason: The study measures successor-token preference and ablates heads ranked by induction score, then evaluates few-shot serial recall. It tests related mechanisms and behaviors in larger open-weight models and a new task, rather than reproducing training-time formation and loss measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about induction heads and other ICL mechanisms; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Rows below cover this study's induction-score measurements, lag-based temporal retrieval results, ablations, and serial-recall task results. The paper does not report training trajectories, induction-head formation time, or the loss-curve bump.
record.test_reason: In 7–9B open-weight models from four families, base and instruct, the study measures per-head induction scores and next-token preference for the successor of a repeated token ([A][B]…[A]→[B]). It also ablates induction-scored heads against random heads. These are its own results on whether induction heads and induction behaviour appear across model families (V4). The base vs instruct contrast gives limited evidence on training setup (V5). It does not study small attention-only models, training dynamics or loss by token index.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that induction-scored heads play a mechanistically specific role in successor-style (lag +1) temporal retrieval and few-shot serial recall in 7–9B LLMs, via a circuit distributed across depth. Random-head ablation often increased lag +1, which they read as possible competing circuitry. They found instruction tuning had a modest effect except for Mistral, and heterogeneity across families. They limit claims to temporal and serial-recall tasks and note task- and function-vector mechanisms for more abstract ICL.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the standard induction-score definition and head ablation approach, but studies shuffled-token lag probabilities and few-shot serial recall in 7B–9B base and instruction-tuned models rather than training-time emergence and the original ICL loss measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and base versus instruction-tuned variant change the observed temporal pattern. Zero ablation reduces lag +1 more than mean ablation. Ablation across all layers reduces lag +1 more than restricting ablations to top or bottom halves.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 10-shot verbatim serial-recall task, ablating 50 induction-scored heads collapses lag +1 recall in Qwen base and instruct (0.97→0.00). It drops Llama-I to 0.28, against 0.90 for random ablation. At 100 heads, random ablation also collapses recall in some models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In 7–8B LLMs, induction-scored heads are needed for few-shot verbatim sequence copying more than random heads are.

record.problems: The study uses 500 frequent English words and notes results may differ with other token sets. It tests models of 7B–9B parameters, not the largest models. Mistral and Gemma did not reliably learn the serial-recall task, which was evaluated only on Llama and Qwen. Several lag-profile results are shown in figures without exact values in the text. The study does not test other ICL tasks or training-time formation.
record.rows_left_out: The induction and random ablation sweeps at head counts other than 100 are not separately recorded for the lag-probability task (Tables A1–A3 and Fig. 4). Serial-recall task values at ablation counts 1, 10, 25, and 100 are omitted (Table A4; only baseline and 50-head comparisons are retained). Layer-restricted and mean-ablation figures are omitted (Figs. A4–A12); the text describes their qualitative outcome under method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: No small attention-only transformers and no test of composition with previous-token heads; only large models are ablated.
No training trajectories, formation window or loss bump.
No measure of loss falling with token index and no broad ICL tasks; only a verbatim serial-recall copy task.
Only 7–9B decoder-only text transformers; other sizes, architectures, modalities and multiple training runs are not tested.
No manipulation of pretraining data, no formation timing and no ICL persistence; only a base vs instruction-tuned comparison.
No non-copying few-shot task learning and no direct test of task or function vectors.

missing.what: After induction-head ablation, base Mistral and Llama (and per the Discussion, Gemma-it) show an increase at lag 0. The authors interpret this as a switch from successor retrieval to copying.
Restricting ablation to the top or bottom half of layers, or using mean ablation, reduces lag +1 less than zero ablation across all layers, consistently across models.

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were removed because these are large models and no composition is tested. The serial-recall rows were unlinked from V3 and V6: the task is verbatim copying, which V6 explicitly concedes to induction heads, so the record's V6 'challenges' label was wrong. Instruct ablation tables start at 1 head, so the 1-head values serve as references. The lag-profile states for S1–S8 rest on the text's descriptions of figures.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests the functional contribution of induction-score-ranked heads to successor retrieval, but not composition with a previous-token head or formation in small attention-only transformers.
No training-time formation window, abruptness, in-context-learning gain over training, or loss-curve bump is measured.
Tests induction-head ablation in a few-shot serial-recall task, not most forms of ICL or loss falling with token index in large transformers.
Tests four model families of roughly 7B–9B parameters and base/instruction-tuned variants. Does not test other sizes, architectures, modalities, or multiple training runs.
Compares base and instruction-tuned variants; does not manipulate training data or systematically measure formation timing or persistence of ICL.
Tests only few-shot serial recall, not other few-shot task-learning settings or alternative mechanisms directly.
No formation trajectory or sequence of formation sub-steps is measured.

relationships.reason: Induction-scored heads are present in all four families (S25–S32). These variants show a lag +1 peak (S4–S6, S8). Ablating induction heads cuts it while random ablation does not (S11, S14–S16 vs S19, S22–S24).
relationships.display_finding: All tested variants contain induction-scored heads and a lag +1 peak that induction-head ablation reduces while random ablation does not.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Induction scores and successor-retrieval behaviour are present, with targeted ablation effects in these conditions.

relationships.reason: Induction scores are present, but the lag +1 preference is only slight. Induction-head ablation barely changes it (S1, S2, S9, S13), while random ablation raises it (S17, S21).
relationships.display_finding: In Llama-3.1-8B base and instruct, induction scores are present, but the slight lag +1 preference barely changes after induction-head ablation and increases after random ablation.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: V4 concerns presence of induction-behaving heads. Table 1 and Figure 1 show induction scores in both variants; weak aggregate output preference does not show those heads are absent or incomplete.

relationships.reason: The unablated peak is at lag 0 (copying), not lag +1 (S3). The ablation effect is on a value that was never a peak (S10, S18).
relationships.display_finding: In Mistral-7B-v0.1 base, the unablated output peaks at lag 0 rather than lag +1, so the ablation affects a nonpeak lag.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The lag 0 output peak does not negate induction behaviour in individual heads. Table 1 reports a mean induction score of 0.54 ± 0.06, and Figure 1 shows scored heads.

relationships.reason: A lag +1 peak exists (S7), but random-head ablation removes it nearly as much as induction-head ablation (S12, S20). The behaviour is not specific to induction-scored heads here.
relationships.display_finding: In Gemma-2-9b base, random-head ablation removes the lag +1 peak nearly as much as induction-head ablation.

source_check.label: limits_scope

statements.correction: Llama base: 0.00103 unablated, 0.00092 after 100 induction-head ablations, 0.00934 after 100 random-head ablations. Gemma base: 0.07125, 0.00206 and 0.00478 respectively. Table 1 reports positive induction scores in both families.
statements.problem: The reported output effects are correct, but weak or non-specific output effects do not establish an exception to the presence of induction-behaving heads in V4.

statements.correction: Mistral base: peak at lag 0; lag +1 probability 0.00060 unablated, 0.00012 after 100 induction-head ablations, 0.00085 after 100 random-head ablations. Mean induction score: 0.54 ± 0.06.
statements.problem: The output peak and ablation values are correct; absence of a dominant output peak at lag +1 does not establish absence of induction-behaving heads.

statements.correction: Positive induction scores in all four model families and both tuning variants; weak Llama output preference; lag 0 dominance in base Mistral; non-specific lag +1 reduction in base Gemma.
statements.problem: This study supports model differences in causal specificity of output effects, but those differences do not qualify V4's narrower claim that induction-behaving heads appear.

statements.correction: Mistral base output peak: lag 0. Mistral instruct output peak: lag +1. Mean induction scores: base 0.54 ± 0.06; instruct 0.50 ± 0.08. No training-time formation or ICL-persistence measurement.
statements.problem: The Mistral peak shift is correct, but it measures retrieval mode rather than whether or when heads form or whether ICL persists, as specified in V5.

statements.correction: Methods 2.4 scoring prompt: 1,000 commonly used tokens repeated twice. Table 1 base→instruct: Llama 0.34 ± 0.05→0.31 ± 0.05; Qwen 0.26 ± 0.08→0.26 ± 0.07; Gemma 0.45 ± 0.14→0.48 ± 0.13. The 500-word, 5000-permutation protocol measures temporal output probabilities.
statements.problem: The score values are correct, but the stated scoring prompt is wrong; static score differences also do not measure V5's formation, timing or persistence outcomes.

statements.correction: Table 1 reports modest base-versus-instruct mean-score differences in Llama, Qwen and Gemma. No formation trajectories or persistence measurements.
statements.problem: The modest score changes are reported correctly, but they concern score magnitude, not the formation, timing or ICL-persistence outcomes named in V5.

statements.correction: Temporal probability: 500 frequent English words, 5000 permutations. Induction scoring: 1,000 commonly used tokens repeated twice. Few-shot serial recall: 14-token letter lists, 50 prompts. Induction scores are present in all four families; output preference and ablation specificity vary by model.
statements.problem: The numerical results are correct. The summary conflates the temporal-probability prompt with induction scoring and treats downstream output limitations as limitations on head presence.
